note: Illustrative activity sequences for evaluation. They are not resident profiles, stereotypes, a waiting list or evidence that any design works. Design pairings are for testing only.

scenarios.title: Living alone, year-round
scenarios.resident: A permanent resident who wants a compact home, a short walk to the lodge and a clear maintenance routine.
steps: Leave the home through the accessible entrance.
Walk the shared path to the lodge.
Collect a parcel or use the laundry.
Speak to a neighbour without entering a private home.
Return home and close the door.
scenarios.question: Can a solo resident make an ordinary errand and a small social contact without a car?
evidenceNeeded: A resident walkthrough with timings and rest points.
A privacy observation at the porch and living-room edge.

scenarios.title: A couple working remotely
scenarios.resident: Two people who need reliable work space, power and bandwidth without turning the home into an office.
steps: Start two simultaneous calls in separate rooms.
Make coffee without crossing a call.
Walk to the lodge for a shared meeting.
Receive a delivery at the entrance.
End the day without work spreading into the bedroom.
scenarios.question: Can two people work at once without acoustic or circulation conflict?
evidenceNeeded: Measured bandwidth, latency and backup power.
Acoustic separation test between work rooms.

scenarios.title: A seasonal resident
scenarios.resident: A summer and shoulder-season resident who does not need a year-round home and should not pretend a compact cabin is one.
steps: Open the home for the season.
Bring in water and supplies.
Use the lodge for laundry and a shared meal.
Close down water and heat before leaving.
Lock the home and leave the shared path clear.
scenarios.question: Can opening and closing be done safely without relying on a year-round occupant?
evidenceNeeded: Water drain-down and freeze protection review.

scenarios.title: Planning for changing mobility
scenarios.resident: An older resident who wants to stay in the community as mobility changes, without assuming the current plan is accessible.
steps: Arrive by the accessible drop-off.
Reach the entrance without a step.
Move from the bedroom to the bathroom with a mobility aid.
Reach the kitchen and a seated work surface.
Ask for help without crossing a private threshold.
scenarios.question: Can a resident with changing mobility complete the day's essential tasks without a redesign?

scenarios.title: A household that hosts guests
scenarios.resident: A resident who wants occasional family and friends to stay without letting visitors take over the hamlet.
steps: Greet a guest at the shared arrival point.
Give the guest a separate sleeping place.
Share a meal at the lodge.
Manage an extra shower and laundry load.
Say goodbye without a parking or noise conflict.
scenarios.question: Can a guest stay be private and generous without consuming shared capacity?

scenarios.title: Gardening and land stewardship
scenarios.resident: A resident who wants to grow food, compost and care for the forest, with realistic water and wildlife constraints.
steps: Carry tools from storage to the garden.
Water without emptying the fire reserve.
Compost and clean tools.
Share produce at the lodge.
Close the garden against wildlife.
scenarios.question: Can gardening fit the water, fire, wildlife and shared-land rules?
evidenceNeeded: Water budget with a separate fire reserve.
